newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary budget improves but cuts needed - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Hungary budget improves but cuts needed - ministry.

text.p: Hungary still plans to cut budget expenditures by 10 billion forints despite the better-than-planned position of the central state budget, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
"We still believe the 10 billion forint reduction is necessary," Csaba Laszlo, State Secretary of the Finance Ministry, told a news conference.

Laszlo said the central state budget is likely to post a surplus in October but Hungary has not changed its plans to cut expenditures by 10 billion forints to meet the government deficit target for 1996, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.

Otherwise the social security funds' worse-than-expected position could threaten the government deficit target, which is four percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) and was agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Laszlo said.
The government budget includes the central state budget, state funds and the local munipalities.
The government is expected to discuss the Finance Ministry's proposal about the expenditure cuts this week.
The deficit of the social security funds -- pension and health care -- soared to 56 billion forints by the end of August, compared with the 17.8 billion forint target for 1996. @
Laszlo said the central state budget's position is better than planned but corporate tax revenues due after December 20 have an uncertainty, worth 10 to 20 billion forints.

The central state budget posted six billion forint surplus in September, with the deficit standing at 114.8 billion forints at the end of the month, which is only 49.3 percent of the target for whole 1996.
"We believe the budget will post a surplus in October again, but in November and also in December we expect a couple of tens of billions deficit again, due to seasonal factors," Laszlo added. @
